subject: MSA review: proposed audit scope, pen-test window, and evidence cadence
messages:
From: Jason Wu <jason.wu@nexacare.com>
To: hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai, monica.patel@redwood.ai
Cc: procurement@nexacare.com
Date: Tue, 15 Sep 2026 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: Redlines to MSA: audit rights & pen-test language

Hannah / Monica,

Thanks for sending the MSA + Order Form. Our legal and security teams reviewed the security exhibit and came back with three asks we need to close before we can move to countersignature:

1) Audit frequency: we need on-demand audit rights (up to twice per year) plus one scheduled annual SOC 2 review.
2) Pen-test window: we want the right to engage a 3rd-party pen test with at least two weeks' notice; tests must be scheduled within a 30-day window and limited to non-production (or a defined production subset).
3) Evidence cadence: for SOC 2 evidence we need a monthly package during the 90-day ramp and then quarterly evidence thereafter.

We attached suggested redlines to the exhibit (summary in the doc). Can Redwood confirm whether you can accept: (A) limiting ad-hoc audits to security incidents or material changes, (B) a 48-hour emergency notification timeframe for pen tests that impact availability, and (C) a monthly read-only evidence bundle for the first 90 days.

If we can align quickly we will issue an internal PO and route for signature.

Thanks,
Jason
Sr. Security Program Manager
NexaCare

Attachments: NexaCare_redlines_v2.pdf
From: hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai
To: Jason Wu <jason.wu@nexacare.com>
Cc: monica.patel@redwood.ai, jonas.weber@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 15 Sep 2026 10:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Redlines to MSA: audit rights & pen-test language

Jason —

Appreciate the clear list. Quick reactions from our side:

- Audit frequency: we typically allow one on-site or remote audit per 12 months plus an ad-hoc audit tied to a defined incident or regulatory requirement. We can be flexible on a second ad-hoc right if scoped (limited to 1 additional per 12-month period) and with a mutually agreed plan.
- Pen-tests: we can accept a 30-day scheduling window. For production testing we require a written scoping document, mutually agreed impact hours, and a 72-hour notification for standard tests (48 hours for high-priority emergency tests is tight for our ops cadence).
- Evidence cadence: we can provide a monthly "assurance bundle" (read-only artifacts + log digest) during a 90-day onboarding period and move to quarterly thereafter. We propose the bundle be delivered via a secure Share link and include a signed digest to verify integrity.

I'll loop in Jonas (security) and Monica (legal) to propose precise contract language. Suggest a short call tomorrow to resolve outstanding items and agree final redlines.

Best,
Hannah Schmitt
Head of Legal Operations
Redwood Inference

--
redwood_security_exhibit_draft_v3.docx (attached)
From: jonas.weber@redwood.ai
To: Jason Wu <jason.wu@nexacare.com>
Cc: hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai, monica.patel@redwood.ai, laura.bennett@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 16 Sep 2026 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Redlines to MSA: audit rights & pen-test language

Jason / team —

Thanks for the detail. A few technical clarifications from Security so legal can capture them cleanly:

1) Scope: we prefer offering a dedicated read-only audit view (timeboxed) for audits rather than full network access. If NexaCare needs infrastructure-level testing, we can scope a limited production-subset test with a black-box approach.
2) Pen-test impact window: operationally we prefer to define an allowable impact threshold (e.g., no sustained service degradation >2 minutes per hour; outage tests must be pre-approved and limited to a maintenance window).
3) Evidence package contents: SOC 2 summary, control mappings, configuration snapshots (redacted where needed), and a signed log digest (SHA256). We cannot provide raw customer data; logs will be redacted and access audited.

Proposed compromise for contract language: allow one scheduled audit + one mutually agreed ad-hoc audit per 12 months; pen-test with two-week notice and 30-day window; evidence bundle monthly for 90 days, then quarterly. I'll attach the SOC2_coverage_summary.pdf and a short pen-test statement.

If that matches what you need, Hannah/Monica can convert to redline language. If not, please call out the specific clauses you need kept.

—Jonas
Director, Security Engineering
Redwood Inference

Attachments: SOC2_coverage_summary.pdf, pen_test_statement.pdf
From: monica.patel@redwood.ai
To: Jason Wu <jason.wu@nexacare.com>
Cc: hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai, jonas.weber@redwood.ai, laura.bennett@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 16 Sep 2026 13:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Redlines to MSA: audit rights & pen-test language

Jason —

Following Jonas' technical points, we drafted proposed redline snippets for the MSA exhibit. Highlights:

- Audit rights clause: "Customer may request one scheduled audit per 12 month period and, subject to mutual agreement and operational scoping, one additional ad-hoc audit in the same 12 month period. Audits will be conducted via a timeboxed, read-only audit view unless otherwise agreed in writing."

- Pen-test clause: "Customer may perform third-party penetration testing with two weeks' advance notice. Tests must be scoped and approved in writing; tests affecting production availability are restricted to mutually agreed maintenance windows and must not exceed agreed impact thresholds."

- Evidence cadence clause: "During the first 90 days following go-live, Provider will deliver a monthly assurance bundle (SOC 2 summary, control mappings, redacted configuration snapshots, and a signed log digest). Thereafter, Provider will deliver the bundle quarterly. Emergency evidence requests tied to incidents will be addressed per the incident response SLA."

Two asks from NexaCare that we could negotiate: (1) they are asking for the ability to substitute one of the scheduled audits for a second ad-hoc audit at any time — we should limit that to incident/regulatory triggers; (2) they want 48 hour notice for emergency pen-tests — we should push back to 72 hours but accept 48 for true emergencies with an exception process.

If you agree, I'll prepare a marked MSA exhibit we can send back with track changes. Otherwise propose specific alternative language.

Thanks,
Monica Patel
Sr. Counsel, Contracts
Redwood Inference

--
Proposed redline snippets included in attachments.
From: Jason Wu <jason.wu@nexacare.com>
To: monica.patel@redwood.ai, hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai
Cc: procurement@nexacare.com
Date: Fri, 17 Sep 2026 15:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Redlines to MSA: audit rights & pen-test language

Monica / Hannah —

Appreciate the proposed language and the flexibility on the evidence bundle. The proposed audit cap (one scheduled + one ad-hoc tied to incidents) is acceptable as long as "ad-hoc" can be initiated with a documented security rationale (we'll capture that in the purchase order). On pen-tests, NexaCare can accept 72-hour standard notification for normal tests; we will reserve the 48-hour emergency option for urgent security investigations only and agree to provide a written justification when invoking it.

Please send the marked exhibit and we'll aim to review within 48 business hours. Once we align, procurement will route the PO and countersign.

Regards,
Jason
Sr. Security Program Manager
NexaCare

--
Next steps: Hannah to upload marked exhibit to Drive; Monica to prepare final redlines; Jonas to confirm signed digest approach; Laura to confirm SOW/Order Form alignment.
